goal: Phase 3 (docs-and-releases) of campaign become-faberun: user-facing documentation replaces evolution-internal notes -- a command manual, the vision, the concepts, a getting-started path, an architecture summary and ADRs -- and release-please cuts versioned GitHub releases from Conventional Commits. Spec: docs/campaigns/become-faberun/spec/SPEC.md.

taskPacket.objective: The supervisor's terminateControllerGroup signals a controller's process group only with proof that the pid still names the controller that wrote the lock (its recorded processStartToken), and an EPERM from that signal never escapes -- closing the one remaining path the stale-group guard of phase 2 left open.
instructions: Read src/engine/supervise.mjs `terminateControllerGroup`: it reads the run lock, decides the target is alive with `pidAlive(target) || groupAlive(target)` -- both true for a recycled pid, and groupAlive even returns true on EPERM -- then sends SIGTERM and SIGKILL to -pid, and its default kill rethrows any non-ESRCH error. The lock record already carries `processStartToken` (src/run/lock.mjs writes it and uses it for staleness), so the proof exists and is unused. Read src/engine/process-identity.mjs (`invocationOwned`, the phase-2 guard) and src/run/lock.mjs (`processStartToken`, `pidAlive`, the staleness check) so the supervisor asks the same question the engine now asks.

Change terminateControllerGroup: before any signal, require that the lock's pid answers `process.kill(pid, 0)` without EPERM and that, when the lock records a processStartToken, `processStartToken(pid)` still equals it; a lock without a token is treated as unverifiable and is NOT signalled -- the function returns false and the caller proceeds as if the group were already gone (the takeover path already handles a dead controller). Treat EPERM from the group signal and from the pid fallback exactly like ESRCH: not ours or gone, never thrown. Reuse `invocationOwned` from process-identity.mjs by shaping the lock record as an invocation probe ({pid, processGroupId: pid, processStartToken}) rather than writing a second identity check.

Tests in test/engine/supervise.test.mjs: (a) a lock naming `process.pid` with a fabricated token makes terminateControllerGroup return false without signalling (if it signalled, the test runner would die -- that is the production defect); (b) an injected kill that throws EPERM is swallowed and the function returns false; (c) the existing cases where a real detached fixture controller is terminated keep passing, with the fixture lock carrying the real token. Do not run test/engine/supervise.test.mjs yourself: inside the dsh sandbox process-signalling tests hang until the executor's cap. Run only tsc and test/repo/source-shape.test.mjs; the controller runs the supervise tests as this node's verification.
Run the two commands you may run in the foreground, fix what they report, and report done.
decisions: The supervisor proves ownership through the lock's processStartToken via invocationOwned; no token means no signal.
EPERM is handled like ESRCH everywhere in the supervisor path.
The worker never runs process-signalling tests inside the dsh sandbox; the controller's verification is the proof.
nonGoals: Do not change relaunch thresholds, heartbeat semantics or the lock format.
Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself.

definitionOfDone.text: the supervise, heartbeat, lock and source-shape tests pass under the controller
tsc is clean
terminateControllerGroup signals only with a matching start token and never lets EPERM escape; the fabricated-token test proves it without killing the runner

taskPacket.objective: Every push to main lets release-please maintain a release pull request from the Conventional Commits; merging it tags vX.Y.Z, publishes a GitHub Release, bumps package.json, and the same workflow publishes that version to npm as `faberun` through npm trusted publishing (OIDC, no token) -- the tags install.sh and faberun update already consume, and the package `npm install -g faberun` installs.
instructions: Read the 'Distribution' decision in docs/campaigns/become-faberun/spec/SPEC.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml and pr-policy.yml (the gates a release PR must pass: non-blank body, title plus body valid under commitlint, every commit valid), and test/host/ci-policy.test.mjs (the test that pins the workflows).

Create .github/workflows/release-please.yml: name `release-please`; `on: push: branches: [main]`; `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write`; one job `release-please` on ubuntu-latest with a single step `uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4` and `with: token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}, config-file: release-please-config.json, manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json`. No checkout step is needed by the action; add none.

Create .github/workflows/release-please.yml with two jobs. Job `release-please` (ubuntu-latest): a single step `uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4` with `id: release` and `with: token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}, config-file: release-please-config.json, manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json`; it declares `outputs: release_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}` and `tag_name: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag_name }}`. Job `publish-npm` (ubuntu-latest) runs only `if: needs.release-please.outputs.release_created == 'true'` with `needs: release-please` and `permissions: contents: read, id-token: write`: `actions/checkout@v4` with `ref: ${{ needs.release-please.outputs.tag_name }}`, `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: 22` and `registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org`, then `npm publish --provenance --access public` with no token step -- authentication is npm trusted publishing (the package's npm settings name this repository and this workflow file as its trusted GitHub Actions publisher), so `npm publish` exchanges the job's OIDC token itself and no `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` or `NPM_TOKEN` appears anywhere. Top-level `permissions: contents: write, pull-requests: write` stay on the first job; the leading comment of the file names the one-time npm setup (npmjs.com -> package faberun -> Settings -> Trusted publisher -> GitHub Actions: owner feliperun, repository faberun, workflow release-please.yml) and the reservation publish of 0.3.0 that created the package. No checkout is needed by the release-please job; add none there.

Create CHANGELOG.md with the heading `# Changelog`, one sentence saying release-please generates the entries below from Conventional Commits, and a `## 0.3.0 (2026-09-09)` section with one paragraph pointing at docs/history/RETROSPECTIVE-2026-09-08.md as the record of the lean release, so the file has a starting point release-please can append above.

A release PR carries the title `chore(main): release X.Y.Z` and a changelog body: confirm against pr-policy.yml and commitlint.config.mjs that both gates accept it (the type chore with scope main is conventional; the body is non-blank) and state that in the workflow file's leading comment. Change nothing in pr-policy.yml or ci.yml.

Extend test/host/ci-policy.test.mjs with tests for the release pipeline: release-please.yml triggers only on push to main, declares exactly the two write permissions, uses googleapis/release-please-action@v4 with the config and manifest paths; release-please-config.json parses, names package `faberun`, release-type node and include-component-in-tag false; .release-please-manifest.json's `.` equals package.json's version (so a manual bump never desynchronises them); CHANGELOG.md exists and starts with `# Changelog`.

package.json gains `"publishConfig": { "access": "public" }` and keeps `files` as it is (bin, src, skills, integrations); `npm pack --dry-run` must list bin/faberun.mjs, package.json, README.md and the src/, skills/ and integrations/ trees. Nothing else in package.json changes.
Run the verification commands yourself in the foreground with explicit timeouts and fix what they report before reporting done. Do not run the whole suite; the controller does.
decisions: release-please with release-type node, tags vX.Y.Z without a component prefix, 0.x bumping rules.

npm distribution: the same workflow publishes `faberun` to npm on every release through trusted publishing (OIDC + provenance); no token secret exists. The name was reserved by an orchestrator publish of 0.3.0.
The manifest version must always equal package.json's version, enforced by test.
nonGoals: Do not change ci.yml or pr-policy.yml.
Do not bump the version; release-please does. Do not publish from the worktree.
Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself.

taskPacket.objective: docs/VISION.md carries the owner's positioning of Faberun in the agent-kit vision structure, and docs/CONCEPTS.md defines the vocabulary an operator needs -- each term with its definition, where it lives, and the invariant that holds.
instructions: Read the appendix 'positioning (the owner's pitch, verbatim)' and the 'Decisions already made' in docs/campaigns/become-faberun/spec/SPEC.md, DESIGN.md ('Identity' and 'Documentation'), the skill references (rules, contract, operations, handoffs, engineering, workflow) for the exact vocabulary, docs/history/RETROSPECTIVE-2026-09-08.md for why the tool is subtractive, and the two agent-kit templates skills/init-agentkit/templates/docs/VISION.md and ABSTRACTIONS.md for the section structure to follow.

Write docs/VISION.md with the template's sections -- Why this, why now; The problem; The insight; Principles; Near-term horizon; Non-goals (for now); Related docs -- filled from the pitch: model- and harness-agnostic orchestration above the coding agents, software built rather than generated, the transition from making to running, intent kept while tools change. Principles must be the ones the code enforces (closed packets, mechanical proof before judgment, cross-vendor review, no spend ceiling with bounded attempts, history never rewritten, zero runtime dependencies). Near-term horizon: the first Faberun release from this campaign. Keep it opinionated and under 120 lines; no marketing adjectives.

Write docs/CONCEPTS.md as the vocabulary (it replaces the template's ABSTRACTIONS.md): intent, campaign, contract, run, node, task packet and its three modes (execution, discovery, autonomous), worker, judge, gate (advisory, blocking, failOn, revisions), definition of done and its proofs (command, path, verification, judgment), harness versus model versus vendor versus runtime, tier and costRank and fallback, attempt worktree, seal, integration ref and candidate, promotion and the landing branch, final verification and the phase-terminal node, seat, handoff and journal, attention and parked, supervise and resume, evidence (the .runs/ layout). For each term: one paragraph of definition, where it lives (file, directory or command), and the invariant that always holds -- taken from the references, not invented. Cross-link to docs/COMMANDS.md sections and to skills/faberun/references/*.md; links to COMMANDS.md, GETTING-STARTED.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and adr/README.md are expected even though sibling nodes are writing them right now -- the terminal node of this phase runs the link check.
Both files in English, sentence-case headings, `Faberun` in prose and `faberun` for the command, no em dashes or arrows in headings. Do not touch README.md.
Run the verification commands yourself in the foreground with explicit timeouts and fix what they report before reporting done. Do not run the whole suite; the controller does.
decisions: VISION.md follows the agent-kit template structure and carries the owner's pitch; CONCEPTS.md replaces ABSTRACTIONS.md as the vocabulary.
Every invariant in CONCEPTS.md is traceable to a reference document or to the code.
Links to sibling-node documents are allowed; the phase's terminal node runs the link check.

Do not edit README.md or the skill references.
Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself.
